minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 28, 2016

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Pro Tem Bucknum at 5:01 p.m., on June 28, 2016, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on June 23, 2016, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Absent:  Mayor Ury

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

 CS1.  Conference with Legal Counsel Pursuant to Government Code 54957(a) on
  Matters Posing a Threat to Public Services, Facilities and Operations.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 p.m. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The
City Council reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Mayor Ury was
absent.)
City Council Minutes  1  June 28, 2016
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there was nothing to report from Closed Session.

INVOCATION: Council Member Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Proclaim July 2016 as Recreation & Parks Month

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum presented the proclamation to Director of Recreation and
  Community Services Mark Nix and his staff.

 P2.  Mission Viejo Film Festival Presentation

  The presentation will be rescheduled at a future date.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Bob Holtzclaw, Lake Forest: spoke about a volunteer clean-up project at Aliso Creek. He
expressed concerns about the amount of trash and vegetation overgrowth and asked about the
possibility of a joint effort between Mission Viejo and Lake Forest to clean up the creek.

Charlene Goetz and Shelly Peterson, M.V.: announced that the Driving Miz Daisy vintage market
is held at Saddleback College on the second Sunday of every month.

Dave Leckness, M.V.: discussed the threat of the West Nile Virus and Zika Virus.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 4, 6, 8, and 9 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
NOES:  None
ABSENT: Ury

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

City Council Minutes  2  June 28, 2016
   Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of June 14, 2016, as presented.

 5.  Contract Renewal with Age Well Senior Services and California Yellow Cab for
  Senior Mobility Program Transportation

  Approved renewal of contracts for Senior Mobility Program transportation.

 7.  Microsoft Licensing Renewal

  Approved purchase order for year two of three-year agreement with Microsoft for
  Microsoft Product Licensing renewal and issued a purchase order to SoftwareONE
  (Formerly CompuCom) for such services for 2016-17 in the amount of $66,930.83.

 10.  2017 Orange County International Triathlon in Mission Viejo

  Approved the request submitted by Pelican Coast Events LLC to hold the 2017 Orange
  County International Triathlon in Mission Viejo on Sunday, June 4, 2017.

 11.  Trabuco Hills High School 5K Run-Road Closure Request

  Approved the Special Events Permit submitted by Trabuco Hills High School
  authorizing the closure of Mustang Run between Los Alisos and Aguilar and a partial
  closure on Empanada on Saturday, October 29, 2016.

 12.  Safety Lighting LED Conversion-Southern California Edison Territory (CIP 228)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project;
  (2) authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the
  City Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release
  the faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being
  filed with the City; (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the date
  of recordation of the Notice of Completion; (5) authorized the City Manager to execute
  contract Change Order No. 1 to Purchase Order 21600249 with Express Energy Services,
  Inc., in the amount of $15,335.29, and (6) adopted Resolution 16-32 Amending the Fiscal
  Year 2015-2016 Budget for Costs Related to Capital Improvement Project 228.

 13.  Establish an Appropriations Limit for the 2016-17 Fiscal Year

City Council Minutes  3  June 28, 2016
   Adopted Resolution 16-33 Establishing an Appropriations Limit for the 2016-17 Fiscal
  Year.

OLD BUSINESS

 15.  Refinancing of the Lease Revenue Refunding Bonds, 2009 Series A

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum took item 15 out of order so that representatives of Bond
  Counsel could speak on the matter, if necessary, before leaving for the airport.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to (1)
  adopt City of Mission Viejo Resolution 16-34 Approving Proceedings by the Mission
  Viejo Community Development Financing Authority for the Issuance and Sale of Lease
  Revenue Bonds to Refund the Outstanding Mission Viejo Community Development
  Financing Authority Lease Revenue Refunding Bonds, 2009 Series A, and Approving
  Related Documents and Official Actions; and (2) adopt Community Development
  Financing Authority Resolution 16-02 Authorizing the Issuance and Sale of Lease
  Revenue Bonds to Refund the Outstanding Mission Viejo Community Development
  Financing Authority Lease Revenue Refunding Bonds, 2009 Series A, and Approving
  Related Documents and Official Actions.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

 3.  Check Register Dated June 3, 2016 in the Amount of $263,780.47

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about a payment made to Community Services
  Network South Coast Magazine. She asked about the service area for that publication
  and expressed concern that the City is using tax dollars to import people for special
  events.

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg said he will have to get back to her with the information
  requested.

  Council Member Schlicht asked about a payment to Land CM Corp. for a Bicycle
  Corridor Improvement Program.

City Council Minutes  4  June 28, 2016
   Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon responded that this was for consultant services
  for preparation of grant application for the Bicycle Corridor Improvement Program.

  Council Member Schlicht also questioned a payment to Stantec Consulting Services for
  Oso Parkway Study.

  Director Chagnon responded that this was for consultant services for the next phase of
  the Oso Widening Project.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to
  ratify the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

 4.  Check Register Dated June 10, 2016 in the Amount of $1,408,784.51

  Council Member Schlicht asked about a payment made to LPA Inc. for consulting Services
  for City Hall and the Library.

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg responded that LPA was hired to do design work for increased
  security at the public counters at the two buildings.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

 6.  Professional Services Consultant Team

  Council Member Schlicht indicated that she pulled this report from the Consent Calendar
  in error.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to (1)
  approve the Professional Services Consultant Team Roster (for plan check/design or
  other professional services); and (2) authorize the City Manager to execute contracts
  with members of the Professional Services Consultant Team as needed.

City Council Minutes  5  June 28, 2016
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

 8.  2016 Residential Resurfacing—Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays (CIP 838)

  Items 8 and 9 were considered together.

  Council Member Schlicht asked for clarification on which streets will receive slurry seal
  and which ones will receive asphalt overlay.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon explained which areas were scheduled for the
  asphalt repairs and overlays and said that residents can contact Public Works directly if
  they have questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to (1)
  award the construction contract in the amount of $2,164,995.00 to R.J. Noble Company
  for the subject project; and (2) adopt Resolution 16-35 Amending the Fiscal Year 2015-
  2016 Budget for Costs Related to Capital Improvement Project 838.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

 9.  2016 Residential Resurfacing-Slurry Seal (CIP 838)

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to
  approve the bid specifications, subject to minor revisions required by the City Engineer,
  and authorize staff to advertise for construction bids for the subject project.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

 OLD BUSINESS (Continued)

 14.  2016-2017 School Crossing Guard Services

City Council Minutes  6  June 28, 2016
   Council Member Sachs stated that his questions were answered after the last meeting.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Raths, to (1)
  approve the Third Amendment to Contract with American Guard Services, Inc., to
  modify certain terms of the contract; and (2) authorize staff to issue a purchase order to
  American Guard Services, Inc. in the amount of $330,378 for the period July 1, 2016 to
  June 30, 2017 pending approval of the FY 2016-2017 budget.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

 16.  Update on CUSD Bond Measure Issue

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  The following expressed concern with the amount of money the school district is
  proposing for the bond measure and that the district can't identify where the money will
  be spent: Sharon Campbell, M.V. and Wayne Tate, M.V.

  By consensus, the City Council received the report and directed staff to send a letter of
  support in favor of AB2116.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

 17.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

18.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths thanked Bob Holtzclaw for attending the meeting this evening and pointing
out pollution in Aliso Creek. He also asked staff to look into a shade structure for the bocce ball
courts.

City Council Minutes  7  June 28, 2016
 Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs announced that the first community workshop for the Vision Plan will take
place on Thursday, June 30 at 6:30 p.m. in the Saddleback Room at City Hall. It will be the first
of three public meetings in the Vision Plan process and he encouraged residents to attend. He also
announced that the website - envision.cityofmissionviejo.org - has details on the project, map of
the core area, and information on the process. Council Member Sachs announced that he has not
stopped working on the sober living conditions in South County. He noted that an Orange County
Superior Court Judge, in a tentative hearing, declared that a sober living home in Talega (San
Clemente) was not operating as a business and did violate the HOA's rules regarding nuisances.
The Judge ruled that the sober living home could continue to operate as long as the owner requested
a property management license from the City and adhered to the noise, smoking, and conduct
regulations. The Judge also stated that payment for the use of a home is not sufficient to establish
operations of a business and homeowners are free to lease their homes and receive compensation
for that rental but it does not make the home itself a business. Council Member Sachs said that the
City of Mission Viejo is very much in favor of helping people through their issues and medical
problems and conditions, but the Council and staff are also aware of the needs of the residents and
how these sober living homes come into communities and basically rezone the area simply by their
existence.

Council Member Schlicht

 19.  Consideration of Continuation of Media Alert Service

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht and seconded by Council Member Sachs, to
  discontinue the media e-mail alert service known as CustomScoop and look into other
  services and, in the interim, to use Google Alerts.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

 Council Member Schlicht emphasized to residents that the Capistrano Unified School District is
 trying to rush to judgement on the bond issue and they are keeping the public unaware. She noted
 that the City is proposing to lease environmentally-friendly vehicles and she has done some
 research on other options. Council Member Schlicht expressed concern with the upkeep of the
 slopes throughout the City. She stated that since 2005 the City has spent $50 million and it is still
 maintaining dirt and weeds. She said that although it was one of the Council priorities in the
 budget last year, she feels that the slopes are not getting enough attention and that property values
 are affected by the lack of maintenance of the slopes. In conclusion, Council Member Schlicht
 acknowledged the Brexit vote in Great Britain with the following quote by Sir Winston Churchill:
City Council Minutes  8  June 28, 2016
  “Today we may say aloud before an awestruck world, we are still masters of our fate and captains
 of our souls.”

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum announced that on July 18, there will be a Neighborhood Watch and
Public Safety Town Hall Meeting in the Council Chamber from 6:00 to 7:30 p.m. and additional
information will be forthcoming on the City’s website. She asked staff to look into expanding the
creek cleanup program to assist the City of Lake Forest in the Aliso Creek cleanup project. Mayor
Pro Tem Bucknum encouraged residents to attend the Vision Plan Workshop on Thursday June 30
and she also invited residents to attend the 4th of July Street Faire.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:09 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, July 12, 2016, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, Assistant City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of July 12, 2016

City Council Minutes  9  June 28, 2016
